text: 25 nurses coming over the next four months. Honestly, good. I'll bake them something. But Central is 40 nurses short right now, tonight, and a virus doesn't wait for a recruitment drive. What keeps a night shift workable isn't more names on the roster next year, it's fewer people getting seriously ill in the same week. That's why I'm voting yes.

New Haven's arts festival has just put out 40 events. In 2021 I sat on the council watching our budget fall apart while every hall in town stayed locked, and I argued against some of those closures. I'd rather this programme actually goes ahead. A vaccine requirement is how a town stays open through an outbreak, not how it shuts. I'm voting yes, grumbling as usual.

Ferry's on reduced runs for a fortnight while they sort the engine. I'm an apprentice at a boatyard and I can tell you a fortnight is optimistic. Out on the islands the clinic is one nurse and a GP once a week, and the boat is how anyone sick gets to a hospital. Not the moment to let a virus run. I'm voting yes.

First case on the island: one traveller, stable, no spread found. Good, and it's exactly the calm before it that you want to use. My first kid was born in 2021 and we barely left the flat for a year. I'm not doing that with two of them. Get ready while it's quiet. I'm voting yes 🙃

In 2021 I cleaned corridors at Central where beds were lined up because the wards were full. Vaccinated or not, everyone ended up in the same corridor, in the same beds, with the same tired nurses. There's one hospital on this island. Keeping it from filling up is the least two-tier thing we can do. I'm voting yes.

My van is the only library some of the ring road towns have. In 2021 it sat in the depot for months and my regulars went without. The rule that worries people is the thing that keeps the van, the school and the shop running when the virus does arrive. Nobody in those towns gets left out of a lockdown that never happens. I'm voting yes.

In 2021 I helped families say goodbye over a video call because they couldn't be in the room. We waited until it was here last time. The doctors are asking us to get ready before, while it's still one case and a traveller. I'd like to never do another funeral on a screen. I'm voting yes.

Neighbour's boy spent a week in intensive care in 2021. Fit young bloke, worked the yards with his dad. There are about 30 ICU beds between both hospitals for the whole country. I can count, and that's not many. Rather we get ahead of this one than queue for a bed. Voting yes.

I marched with the union against the workplace vaccine rules in 2021, and I'd do it again for what they were then. This one is different: the vaccine is free, it starts only once everyone has had a fair chance to get it, under-12s aren't covered and there are medical exemptions. My old mates on the wharf need the port open more than anyone. I'm voting yes this time.
Got stood down when the shopping centre closed in 2021. Worked nights in a warehouse to pay rent. A closed mall pays nobody. A vaccine requirement is a small thing next to a padlock. I'm voting yes.
topic: Work and jobs (NO's "people unable to work")

text: Hundreds of people get on my bus every day and I can't choose who sits behind me. In 2021 I caught it, was off three weeks, and my kids thought I wasn't coming home. I'd take a bit of protection while I keep the city moving. Voting yes, then back on the ring road.
topic: Work and jobs (NO's "people unable to work")

text: Didn't see my grandkids for most of 2021. Now I do the school run in Crown Harbour twice a week, and the little one talks the whole way. Under-12s aren't covered by the requirement, but they're the ones who lost most when schools shut. I'd rather keep their classroom open. I'm voting yes.

No season in 2021. A few of my boys never came back to the game, and you don't get those years back. I want a full season next year, with crowds on the sideline. A vaccine requirement is a better bet for that than another shutdown. I'm voting yes. Training's Tuesday.

in 2021 my residents went months without a visitor. some of them never saw family again. what keeps the doors of an aged-care home open is less virus going round outside it. that's all this is to me. voting yes

I lost my husband to COVID in 2021 and wasn't allowed to be with him at the end. I don't say that for sympathy. I say it because the nurses who rang me that night are still at Central, still short-handed. If a requirement means fewer families get that phone call, it's worth it. I'm voting yes, with love to all of you.

did my last two years of high school on a laptop and missed my formal. now i scan groceries for hundreds of people every weekend shift. a vaccine requirement is genuinely nothing compared to another year online. voting yes 🤷

ngl the reef survey this week made my whole lab happy, less bleaching. our field trips were the first thing cut in 2021 and we did marine bio from a bedroom. i want to be in the water not on zoom. voting yes tbh

People ask if the vaccine is too new. Fair to ask. What we know: the trials show it lowers the risk of serious illness, with no major safety problems so far. The first doses go to health workers and high-risk people, and it's voluntary. I'll be in that first lot. I've seen what full wards look like and I'm voting yes.
topic: Vaccine doubts (settle a worry, grant nothing)

text: Thirty years as an accountant makes you read the fine print. Proof would be a health ministry certificate, paper or digital, separate from the new ID card, and the ID card law doesn't allow health records on it. I'm as grumpy about government as anyone, and I'm voting yes.
topic: Privacy and ID card (settle a worry)

text: Plenty of my passengers in the season are Aussies and Kiwis off the planes. An outbreak in high season would empty the hotels faster than any certificate. Their own recognised certificates would be accepted, same as at home. Keep the buses full and the island open. I'm voting yes.

Drove the van round the ring road towns this week, and every second conversation was someone still making up their mind. Fair enough, it's a big decision. Mine came down to a woman in one of those towns who can't get to Central in a hurry. I'm voting yes for her.
topic: Before Poll 2: deadlock, no NO lead

text: Quiet week at work, and I hope it stays that way. The doctors' advice is to get ready before a virus is spreading, not after. That's how I think about my trade too: you prepare for the hard days while you still can. I'm voting yes.
topic: Before Poll 2: deadlock, no NO lead

text: Two kids under five, and I've done the 2021 version of parenting: one flat, no playgroup, no grandparents. Never again if I can help it. A free vaccine and a certificate is a trade I'll take. I'm voting yes, now excuse me, someone's eating crayons.
Export orders dried up in 2021 and we fed cattle we couldn't sell. Farming's a gamble at the best of times. I'd rather not add another closure to the odds. I'm voting yes.
